findings.title: Address CRUD functions close over stale `user` state — concurrent/repeated address mutations lose data
findings.evidence: const addAddress = async (address) => { if (!user) return; ... setUser({ ...user, addresses: [...(user.addresses || []), data.address] }); } — same pattern in updateAddress (setUser({...user, addresses: user.addresses.map(...)})), deleteAddress and setDefaultAddress. All four spread the `user` captured at render time instead of using functional updates.
findings.suggested_fix: Use functional updates: setUser(prev => prev ? { ...prev, addresses: [...] } : null) in all four address functions, so consecutive awaits (e.g. addAddress then setDefaultAddress) don't overwrite each other's result.

findings.title: Guest-cart merge can silently drop guest items if a push fails, and is not aborted on logout
findings.evidence: const pushGuest = guestItems.map(item => authFetch('/api/cart', {...}).catch(err => console.error('Failed to merge guest cart item', err))); Promise.all(pushGuest).then(() => authFetch('/api/cart', ...)).then(data => { if (Array.isArray(data)) { setCart(data); localStorage.setItem('cart', JSON.stringify(data)); } }) — a failed POST is swallowed, then the authoritative server list unconditionally REPLACES local state, destroying the guest item.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail the merge (keep local state) when any push rejects, e.g. throw inside the catch so Promise.all rejects and the replace is skipped; or re-push failed items.

findings.title: addToCart computes newQty from stale `cart` closure — rapid double-clicks lose a quantity increment
findings.evidence: const existing = cart.find(item => item.id === product.id); ... newQty = Math.min(existing.quantity + quantity, MAX_CART_QUANTITY); saveCart(cart.map(...)) — two synchronous clicks before re-render both read the same `cart`, so the second overwrites the first (qty +1 not +2).
findings.suggested_fix: setCart(prev => ...) functional update and compute newQty inside it; sync to localStorage in an effect or inside the updater.

findings.title: Product fetch has no cancellation/abort — fast navigation between products can render the wrong product
findings.evidence: useEffect(() => { setLoading(true); fetch(`/api/products/${id}`)...then((data) => { setProduct(data); ... }) .catch(() => { setProduct(null); setLoading(false); }); }, [id]) — no `cancelled` flag or AbortController; a slow response for the previous id resolves last and overwrites the current product (also re-appends stale JSON-LD).
findings.suggested_fix: Add `let cancelled = false;` + guard in then/catch with cleanup, or AbortController aborted in the effect cleanup (compare Offers.tsx which does this correctly).

findings.title: Live-search fetch results not guarded against out-of-order responses
findings.evidence: const timer = setTimeout(() => { fetch(`/api/products?search=...`).then(...setResults(data)...) }, 180); return () => clearTimeout(timer); — timer is cleaned up, but a slow in-flight fetch for an earlier query can resolve after a newer one and overwrite `results` with stale matches.
findings.suggested_fix: Track the latest query in a ref (or use AbortController per effect run) and ignore responses whose query !== latest.

findings.title: Toast removal setTimeout never cleared — state update after unmount / no cleanup on provider teardown
findings.evidence: setTimeout(() => { setToasts((prev) => prev.filter((t) => t.id !== id)); }, 3000); — fire-and-forget timer, not stored or cleared. Harmless for the app-root provider but each toast schedules an untracked timer.
findings.suggested_fix: Store timer ids in a ref Map and clear on unmount; low impact since ToastProvider lives at root.

findings.title: Bot-reply setTimeout not cleared on unmount — setState after unmount if widget closes/user navigates mid-'typing'
findings.evidence: setIsTyping(true); setTimeout(() => { ... setMessages(prev => [...prev, botMsg]); setIsTyping(false); }, 800); — no timer ref/cleanup.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep timer in a ref and clearTimeout in the component's unmount effect.

findings.title: OTP countdown interval leaks on unmount and stacks when startCountdown is called twice
findings.evidence: const startCountdown = (sec = 120) => { setOtpCountdown(sec); const interval = setInterval(() => { setOtpCountdown((prev) => { if (prev <= 1) { clearInterval(interval); return 0; } return prev - 1; }); }, 1000); }; — interval only self-clears via the updater; no cleanup return, and a second send-OTP creates a second concurrent interval.
findings.suggested_fix: Hold the interval in a ref, clearInterval the previous one at the start of startCountdown, and clear it in a useEffect cleanup.

findings.title: setTimeout(() => setAdded(false), 2000) not cleaned up on unmount (same in VipClubBanner.tsx:26, static/Blog.tsx:438)
findings.evidence: addToCart(product); setAdded(true); ... setTimeout(() => setAdded(false), 2000); — a card unmounted within 2s of add-to-cart schedules a setState on a dead component.
findings.suggested_fix: Clear the timeout in a useEffect cleanup (timer ref), or use a small useTimedFlag hook shared by these three sites.

findings.title: Header login modal has no role="dialog", no aria-modal, no focus trap, no Escape close
findings.evidence: <div className="fixed inset-0 z-[9999] flex items-center justify-center p-4 sm:p-6 overflow-y-auto"> — no role/aria-modal attributes anywhere in the file (grep shows only body-overflow effects at lines 29-41); focus is never moved into the modal nor trapped, so keyboard/SR users can tab into background content and Escape does not close it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label, autofocus the first field, trap Tab within the panel, close on Escape (CartDrawer.tsx and Blog.tsx already do this).

findings.title: Cart drawer has role=dialog/aria-modal but no focus management
findings.evidence: <div className="fixed inset-0 z-50 overflow-hidden" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="cart-drawer-title"> — Escape close exists (lines 22-31) but focus is neither moved into the drawer on open nor returned to the trigger on close, and Tab can escape into the page behind the modal.
findings.suggested_fix: Focus the close button on open, implement a Tab cycle (or use <dialog>/inert on background), and restore focus to the opener on close.

findings.title: App shell hardcodes dark canvas #090d16, drifting from --color-canvas-dark #0a1128
findings.evidence: className="min-h-screen ... bg-[#f8fafc] dark:bg-[#090d16]" while index.css:58 defines --color-canvas-dark: #0a1128 (and index.css:131 paints body with var(--color-canvas-dark)). Additional drift: Header.tsx:81 dark:bg-[#080d15]/90, CartDrawer.tsx:69 dark:bg-[#0c1017], LatestReviews.tsx:81 dark:bg-[#0d121c] — four different near-black surfaces vs the token.
findings.suggested_fix: Use bg-[var(--color-canvas-light)] dark:bg-[var(--color-canvas-dark)] in Layout and consolidate the Header/CartDrawer/LatestReviews hardcoded hexes onto the surface tokens.

findings.title: Hardcoded text color dark:text-[#f7f8f8] duplicates --color-text-main-dark instead of referencing the token
findings.evidence: className="... text-zinc-900 dark:text-[#f7f8f8] ..." (also Products.tsx:79,92) — #f7f8f8 is the literal value of --color-text-main-dark (index.css:78), copy-pasted rather than tokenized.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with dark:text-[var(--color-text-main-dark)] so a future palette change propagates.

findings.title: User-visible cart-limit toasts render English digits (۹۹ shown as 99)
findings.evidence: addToast(`حداکثر تعداد مجاز (${MAX_CART_QUANTITY} عدد) در سبد خرید قرار دارد`, 'warning'); and `حداکثر تعداد مجاز ${MAX_CART_QUANTITY} عدد می‌باشد` — MAX_CART_QUANTITY (constants.ts:13 = 99) is interpolated raw, unlike the rest of the UI which uses toPersianDigits.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap with toPersianDigits(MAX_CART_QUANTITY) — import from lib/utils like other components.

findings.title: Brand CTA orange (#F47C20) with white text is 2.7:1 — documented but still used widely on buttons/badges (AA fail for normal text on Obsidian/light canvases)
findings.evidence: index.css comment: "primary-container #F47C20 = CTA fills (white text 2.7:1, large/bold only)" — yet bg-orange-500 text-white appears throughout (e.g. ProductFilterSidebar.tsx:192,192 'bg-orange-500 text-white', :265 'bg-orange-500 text-white border-orange-500') for small filter chips/labels, not only large/bold text.
findings.suggested_fix: Use --color-primary-500 #d94e06 (4.16:1) or --color-primary-700 #994700 (6.12:1) for small white-on-orange text; reserve #F47C20 for large/bold or non-text elements.

findings.title: Server cart mutation responses ignored — local optimistic state can disagree with server (stock-limited qty)
findings.evidence: await authFetch('/api/cart', { method: 'POST', ... body: JSON.stringify({ productId: product.id, quantity }) }); — response body is never read; the server clamps quantity to stock/max-10 (per API spec) but the local cart keeps the requested quantity, so checkout totals can diverge until the next full fetch.
findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile from the POST/PUT response (or refetch cart) when the server-returned item differs from the optimistic one.

findings.title: Client filter cache never invalidated — stale prices/stock served all session after any admin change
findings.evidence: const clientFilterCache = new Map<string, {...}>(); (module scope) ... clientFilterCache.set(cacheKey, { products: data, total: count, totalPages: pages }); — entries live for the whole SPA session; Compare.tsx explicitly refetches for this reason, but the Products page serves cached rows indefinitely.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a TTL (e.g. 60s) or bust the cache on visibilitychange/focus.

findings.title: Context value object recreated every render — all addToast consumers re-render on every toast add/remove
findings.evidence: <ToastContext.Provider value={{ addToast }}> — a new object identity each render of ToastProvider; with ~35 files consuming toasts, each toast's 3s expiry re-renders every subscribed subtree (CartContext/AuthContext providers and their children are descendants).
findings.suggested_fix: useMemo the value ({ addToast }) — addToast is already useCallback'd, so the memo makes the value stable and eliminates cascade re-renders.
